summary: Created 4-phase plan (2.5h) extending guard-destructive-git.sh with three over-staging detectors plus two prose fixes. Confirmed research's core verdicts empirically: no git-snapshot.sh exemption needed, no settings.json change (hook already registered). Found two issues research's manual regex trace missed: a real quoted-commit-message false positive, and an implicit design fork on snapshot-marker interaction.
decisions_made: No settings.json change: hook already registered as PreToolUse/Bash in agent-system/extensions/core/root-files/settings.json:52 (not templates/ as the delegation context suggested); extending it needs no re-registration.

New detectors must block INDEPENDENTLY (own exit 2, own remediation) placed after the clean-tree gate but before the MATCHED chain, so a fresh snapshot marker never exempts over-staging. Naive append to the MATCHED chain would wrongly exempt it and emit wrong remediation text.
Quote-stripping required before flag-scanning: 'git commit -m "fix -a regression"' false-positives without it (empirically confirmed, 13/13 pass with it).
Use --all([[:space:]]|$) over research's --all\b to match the file's existing boundary idiom.

skill-project-overview SKILL.md:435 justified as broken-on-its-own-terms (/.claude/ is gitignored, so 'git add .claude/' stages nothing and warns), NOT as hook-blocked - it is not one of the three blocked forms.
Durable test harness kept out of scope per research; Phase 3 verifies against the real hook without adding a permanent file.
dead_ends: Do not build a marker/allowlist/caller-identification exemption for git-snapshot.sh: verified both segment-extraction patterns return no match against the literal 'bash .claude/scripts/git-snapshot.sh --branch 884', so the hook structurally cannot observe the internal git add -A.
